newsitem.title: MEXICO: Left-wing PRD is second force in Mexican chamber.
newsitem.headline: Left-wing PRD is second force in Mexican chamber.

text.p: The left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) has become the second force in Mexico's lower house of Congress after landmark elections that broke the ruling party's long-held absolute majority, official results showed on Monday.

Results from Mexico's Federal Electoral Institute (IFE) that are still subject to appeal showed the governing Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its 68-year overall majority in the chamber of deputies, winning 239 seats in the 500-seat house.
But they also showed that the PRD, with 125 deputies, has overtaken the conservative National Action Party (PAN), which tallied 122 after the July 6 mid-term election.
The ecologist party PVEM won eight seats and the PT workers party won six, IFE said. IFE has to settle any appeals by Aug. 23 before it can give definitive results.
IFE also said voter turnout totalled 58 percent of the 52 million strong electorate -- some political analysts had predicted a turnout of more than 80 percent.
Monday's figures included the 200 seats allocated on the basis of proportional representation. Last week the IFE published only figures for the 300 directly elected posts.
